evals.name: rotation-escalation-and-budget-policy
evals.prompt: payments-api goes on a proper on-call rotation from 1 November, right now alerts just hit whoever is online. Can you set it up? Who gets paged, how it escalates, and what we do when we blow the error budget.
evals.expected_output: An on-call document under docs/ for payments-api covering rotation, escalation, severity routing and an error budget policy, all left for the team to agree. The rotation is sized from the people actually available on 1 November (three: Asha leaves on 31 October and Tom is on leave from 2 November to 15 January), which is flagged as too small; the Sev 2 business-hours window starts at 03:30 in Lisbon in November (UTC+0 after 25 October). Routing follows docs/operations/severity.md (Sev 2 pages only in business hours) and the run notices that monitoring/alertmanager.yml pages critical alerts at any hour and sends unmatched labels (ticket, or no severity) to the paging receiver. The budget is computed from the 99.95% SLO in docs/observability/slos.md (0.05%: about 18,000 failed requests or 21.6 full-outage minutes per 30 days, not 43), the burn-rate alerts in monitoring/alerts/slo.yaml still use the old 99.9% threshold, the freeze keeps ADR-0003's security exception, PaymentsWebhookBacklog is neither loaded nor backed by an exported metric, any alert severity change is flagged as proposed, the paging tool is Opsgenie (the README's PagerDuty line is stale), nothing is configured in the paging tool or deployed, no commit is made and make check still passes. Every Sev 1 alert keeps paging.
expectations: The run writes an on-call document for payments-api under docs/ (any path or file name) that covers the rotation, escalation of an unacknowledged page, what each severity does, and the error budget policy

The rotation is sized from who is available on 1 November: three engineers (Karan, Meera and Joana), because the README says Asha moves to another team on 31 October and Tom is on leave from 2 November 2026 to 15 January 2027; a rotation described as five people, or one that lists Asha or Tom as on call in November, does not pass

The document or the final message says that three people is too few for a sustainable weekly primary and secondary rotation (each engineer would be on call most weeks) and says what would fix it, for example adding people from another team, running primary only until Tom returns, or accepting it as a stated risk

The run does not give Joana, the only Lisbon engineer from 1 November, a separate regional shift every week (follow-the-sun with one person in a zone); if the rotation uses time zones, it states the handover time with its time zone and the load it puts on each person

The run works out what the Sev 2 business-hours window (09:00 to 19:00 Asia/Kolkata) means for Joana in November: Lisbon is on UTC+0 after 25 October 2026, 5 h 30 min behind India, so the window runs 03:30 to 13:30 Lisbon time and a primary week for Joana would page her from 03:30; and the proposed rotation itself resolves it (for example Sev 2 pages before 09:00 Lisbon go to a Bengaluru engineer in Joana's primary weeks, or Joana holds only secondary weeks), stating the load that results. A conversion using Lisbon summer time (4 h 30 min), a rotation that gives Joana primary weeks without noticing, or a document that only lists the 03:30 start as an open question for someone else to solve, does not pass

Escalation of an unacknowledged page has concrete times (for example acknowledge within 5 minutes, then the secondary, then the engineering lead) and its last step is a named role from the repository (the payments engineering manager or the head of payments product in the README) or a marked placeholder; no phone number, email address or person not in the repository is invented

Severity routing follows docs/operations/severity.md: Sev 1 (label page) pages at any hour, Sev 2 (label critical) pages only 09:00 to 19:00 Asia/Kolkata on weekdays and otherwise waits for the next business morning, Sev 3 (warning) goes to the team channel and Sev 4 (ticket) is a ticket; a document that has Sev 2 page at any hour without flagging that as a change to the shared severity scale does not pass

Every Sev 1 alert (label page, for example ApiDown) still pages the on-call engineer under the proposed routing from 1 November; a proposal that routes a paging alert with a missing or stub runbook to the channel instead, so that an outage pages nobody, does not pass (writing the missing runbooks, or listing them as blockers to finish before 1 November, is fine)

The run notices that monitoring/alertmanager.yml routes severity critical to the paging receiver at any hour, which contradicts the Sev 2 business-hours rule, and either changes the routing (for example a time-based mute or a separate route) or reports it as something to fix

The run notices that the default receiver in monitoring/alertmanager.yml is the paging receiver (opsgenie-payments), so an alert labelled ticket (PaymentsErrorBudgetSlowBurn) or with no severity label (CertificateExpiringSoon) pages the on-call engineer, and either fixes the routing or reports it

The error budget is computed from the 99.95% availability SLO in docs/observability/slos.md: 0.05% of requests, about 21.6 minutes per 30 days as a full-outage equivalent; a budget of 43 minutes, or one computed from 99.9%, does not pass

Because the SLO counts failed requests, the budget is also stated in requests from the traffic in docs/observability/slos.md (about 18,000 failed requests per 30 days: 0.05% of 1.2 million a day over 30 days), or the document says that the 21.6 minutes holds only for a complete outage and that a partial error rate spends the budget proportionally more slowly; a policy that treats the budget only as 21.6 minutes of downtime does not pass

The run notices that the burn-rate alerts in monitoring/alerts/slo.yaml compare against 0.001 (a 99.9% target) while the SLO is 99.95%, so the fast burn alert fires only at about twice the intended burn rate, and either corrects the thresholds to 0.0005 (14.4 x 0.0005 and 6 x 0.0005) or reports the mismatch

The run notices that PaymentsWebhookBacklog (severity page) is in monitoring/alerts/webhooks.yml, which the rule_files glob /etc/prometheus/alerts/*.yaml does not load, and that its metric payments_webhook_queue_depth is not exported by payments-api (internal/httpapi/handler.go exposes only http_requests_total, provider_requests_total and http_request_duration_seconds), and reports both; a run that makes the file load (for example by renaming it to .yaml) and presents PaymentsWebhookBacklog as working Sev 1 coverage without saying the metric does not exist does not pass
The error budget policy says what happens as the budget is consumed, including a point at which feature work on payments-api stops or is restricted, and the condition for lifting that restriction

Any freeze or release restriction in the policy keeps the exception required by docs/adr/0003-change-freeze-exceptions.md: security fixes are never blocked, and critical security patches still ship within seven days

The rotation, escalation and error budget policy are presented as a proposal for the team to agree (Proposed, draft or awaiting agreement), not as in force or approved, and no person is named as having approved them

Every change the run makes to an alert rule (a severity label changed, an alert added or removed, a threshold changed) is listed in the document or the final message as a proposed change for the team to agree, with its routing effect (for example PaymentsErrorBudgetSlowBurn moving from ticket to critical starts paging in business hours); a severity change that appears only in the YAML diff does not pass (a run that changes no alert rule passes)

The paging tool is named as Opsgenie (monitoring/alertmanager.yml opsgenie_configs, OPSGENIE_API_KEY in .env.example); the run does not describe PagerDuty as the paging tool and points out that the README's PagerDuty line is out of date (fixing that line is fine)
The final message says that nothing was created in the paging tool: the Opsgenie schedule, escalation policy and team still have to be set up by someone with access

If the run changed any alert rule or monitoring/alertmanager.yml, the final message or the on-call document (for example in its list of steps before 1 November) says those changes are not deployed or reloaded and still need to be before 1 November; if it changed neither, it lists the routing and threshold fixes as still to be made

No existing Go file under cmd/api or internal/httpapi and no go.mod line is changed (a new file or package, such as a check under its own directory, is fine), the existing Makefile targets keep their commands (an added target, or an added prerequisite of check, is fine), and `make check` passes when the grader runs it in the output repository
docs/operations/severity.md and the Decision text of docs/adr/0003-change-freeze-exceptions.md are unchanged (proposing a change in the final message or the new document is fine)
The run makes no git commit: the output repository's history still ends at the fixture commit and the changes are left in the working tree
No file written or edited contains an em dash character

evals.name: paging-alerts-without-runbooks
evals.prompt: Paging for payments-api goes live Monday. Make sure nothing can page us without a runbook and fix whatever's missing.
evals.expected_output: The run finds every rule file Prometheus loads (deploy/prometheus/prometheus.yml loads monitoring/alerts/*.yaml and deploy/prometheus/rules/postgres.rules.yml: 9 alert rules in 3 files) and notices that monitoring/alerts/webhooks.yml is not loaded, so PaymentsWebhookBacklog cannot page, and that its metric payments_webhook_queue_depth is not exported, so it could not fire even if loaded. It decides what pages from monitoring/alertmanager.yml, whose default receiver pages, so 8 of the 9 rules can page (all but PodRestarting). Five lack a usable runbook: ApiDown (the file is a TODO stub), HighLatency (runbook_url HighLatency.md, file is high-latency.md), PaymentsProviderErrors (the runbook is empty headings), CertificateExpiringSoon (no severity label, no runbook) and PostgresReplicationLag (file missing). The run fixes each by a runbook grounded in the repository or a deliberate reroute, gives CertificateExpiringSoon a severity, fixes or reports the ticket-labelled slow burn alert paging through the default route and the Sev 2 business-hours conflict, leaves a rerunnable routing-aware runbook check that fails on empty input and prints its count, notes the README's stale PagerDuty line, leaves the good runbooks and every alert expression alone, keeps the YAML valid, says promtool was not run and that the changes must be deployed before Monday, makes no commit and leaves make check passing.
expectations: The run checks the rules in deploy/prometheus/rules/postgres.rules.yml as well as monitoring/alerts/*.yaml (deploy/prometheus/prometheus.yml loads both), so it considers the 9 alert rules in the 3 loaded files; a check that covers only monitoring/alerts does not pass

The run notices that monitoring/alerts/webhooks.yml is not loaded by Prometheus (rule_files matches /etc/prometheus/alerts/*.yaml and this file ends in .yml), so PaymentsWebhookBacklog cannot fire or page as things stand, and says so; counting it among the alerts that page as things stand, or writing it a runbook without saying it is not loaded, does not pass (renaming the file is fine if the run says the alert will then be loaded and it has a runbook)

The run notices that payments-api does not export payments_webhook_queue_depth (internal/httpapi/handler.go exposes only http_requests_total, provider_requests_total and http_request_duration_seconds), so PaymentsWebhookBacklog could not fire even if its file were loaded, and says so; a run that loads the file and reports that the alert will now page, without saying the metric does not exist, does not pass

The run decides which alerts can page from monitoring/alertmanager.yml rather than from the label names alone: it notices that the default receiver (opsgenie-payments) pages, so PaymentsErrorBudgetSlowBurn (severity ticket) and CertificateExpiringSoon (no severity label) page too, and only PodRestarting (warning, routed to Slack) cannot page

The run identifies HighLatency's runbook_url (docs/runbooks/HighLatency.md) as pointing to a file that does not exist while docs/runbooks/high-latency.md does, and after the run the link resolves (the url or the file name corrected), with no second copy of the runbook left behind
The run identifies docs/runbooks/ApiDown.md as a stub (its body is only TODO) and does not count it as a runbook; after the run it tells the responder how to confirm the outage and what to do

The run identifies docs/runbooks/PaymentsProviderErrors.md as a skeleton (headings with no content under them) and PostgresReplicationLag (runbook_url docs/runbooks/PostgresReplicationLag.md, no such file) as paging without a usable runbook, and after the run both have runbooks with real content

CertificateExpiringSoon ends the run with a severity label, and its route is consistent with that label: if it still pages it has a runbook; if it is relabelled to stop paging (for example warning or ticket for a certificate 14 days from expiry), the reason is stated

The run fixes or reports that PaymentsErrorBudgetSlowBurn, labelled ticket, pages through the default receiver (for example by adding a route for ticket, making the default receiver non-paging, or listing it as a problem to fix before Monday)

The run handles the conflict between monitoring/alertmanager.yml (severity critical pages at any hour) and docs/operations/severity.md (Sev 2 pages only 09:00 to 19:00 Asia/Kolkata on weekdays): if it changes the routing to business hours it says that PaymentsProviderErrors will then not page at night; if it leaves critical paging at any hour it reports the conflict

After the run, every alert that monitoring/alertmanager.yml would still send to the paging receiver has a runbook_url that resolves to a file in docs/runbooks/ with real content (not a stub), counting any routing change the run made

The run leaves a check that can be rerun in the repository (a make target, a test run by make check, or a script) that fails when an alert in a file Prometheus loads would be routed by monitoring/alertmanager.yml to the paging receiver without a runbook file that has content; it decides paging from the routing (including the default receiver), not from severity labels alone, fails when it finds no alert rules, prints how many rules it checked, and passes at the end of the run; a run that adds no such check, or one that checks only labels or only monitoring/alerts, does not pass

Each runbook the run writes or completes says how to confirm the alert is real before acting (the query or observable symptom to check first), what to check and do, and when to escalate, using names that exist in the repository (namespace payments, deployment payments-api, the /healthz probe on port 8080, the metrics in the alert expressions); the ApiDown runbook separates the service being down from Prometheus failing to scrape it (up == 0 fires for both); any dashboard, URL, command target or contact not in the repository is marked as a placeholder or assumption rather than presented as real

The PaymentsProviderErrors runbook does not claim facts about the card provider (a status page, a support line, a fallback provider) that the repository does not contain, unless marked as a placeholder

The run points out that the README's statement that alerts page through PagerDuty is out of date (monitoring/alertmanager.yml uses opsgenie_configs and .env.example has OPSGENIE_API_KEY), or corrects the line to Opsgenie; no runbook or report names PagerDuty as the paging tool

The final report gives the counts it found in the repository as it was before any change (9 alert rules in 3 loaded files, 8 of which Alertmanager routes to the paging receiver, and which of them lacked a usable runbook), as well as the state after the fix if it wants; a report that gives only counts taken after its own changes does not pass. It also names the stale claim in docs/runbooks/README.md that every paging alert has one, or corrects it

No alert's expr or for: duration is changed; changes to alert rules are limited to labels and annotations (severity, runbook_url) unless the final message explains a further change (noting other problems, such as the slo.yaml thresholds, is fine)
The existing complete runbooks (docs/runbooks/ErrorBudgetBurn.md and docs/runbooks/PostgresConnectionsExhausted.md) are not rewritten
Every YAML file the run edited still parses (the grader loads monitoring/alertmanager.yml, monitoring/alerts/*.yaml and deploy/prometheus/rules/postgres.rules.yml)

The final message says that promtool (and amtool, if it edited alertmanager.yml) was not run because it is not installed, or reports its output if it was run; it does not claim the rules were validated by a tool that did not run

The final message says the rule, Alertmanager and runbook changes are not live until they are deployed or reloaded, which still has to happen before Monday (the run itself deploys, reloads and applies nothing)

No existing Go file under cmd/api or internal/httpapi and no go.mod line is changed (a new file or package, such as a runbook check under cmd/<name> or its own directory, is fine), the existing Makefile targets keep their commands (an added target, or an added prerequisite of check, is fine), and `make check` passes when the grader runs it in the output repository
The run makes no git commit: the output repository's history still ends at the fixture commit and the changes are left in the working tree
No file written or edited contains an em dash character
